subject: Deployment mode and migration plan - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-medtech.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-medtech.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode and migration plan - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Olivia / Samir -

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to learn more about Acme's roadmap for integrating LLMs into your clinical workflows. Quick recap from our side and a few next steps so we can scope a pilot that matches your constraints: 

Summary of requirements I heard:
- Low-latency inference for clinician-facing flows (target P95 < 250ms for short prompts)
- Peak concurrency ~15-20 qps, steady-state ~5 qps
- PHI will need to stay in a controlled environment (HIPAA concern) for a subset of requests; other requests are non-PHI
- Prefer predictable cost and throughput; currently using OpenAI API for prototyping and some in-house k8s GPU tests
- Timeline: pilot in ~6 weeks if we can agree on scope and compliance guardrails

Deployment-mode options we discussed (and suggested approach):
1) Hosted API - fastest to get started for non-PHI traffic, quick time-to-value, Redwood-managed.
2) Dedicated capacity - reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput & SLAs; good fit if you want committed performance for production (can host non-PHI + some isolated traffic).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) - required for any PHI workloads where you control the network/KMS; longer lead time for onboarding.

Given your mix of PHI + non-PHI and desire for predictable throughput, I recommend a hybrid pilot: dedicated capacity for production non-PHI traffic + a Private VPC sandbox for PHI workflows (or dedicated with customer-managed VPC peering if you want a single plane). We can also run an initial migration plan from OpenAI API to Redwood Dedicated to validate latency/costs before moving PHI traffic.

Attached: initial SOW draft and SOC2 summary for review.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the qps and P95 targets above? (Olivia/Samir)
- Can Samir share a high-level network diagram and security contact for PHI onboarding?
- Would you like David (our SE) to run a short benchmark against your representative prompts?
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sync next week with Samir + David to walk migration plan and pilot scope.

If that sounds good I'll send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks -

Marissa Cole
Account Executive - Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0127

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (stub), SOC2-summary.pdf (stub)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-medtech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 12:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Deployment mode and migration plan - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful and captures our needs. A few clarifications from our side:

- QPS / latency: the 15-20 qps peak is correct for the pilot clinician workflow. P95 target is 200-250ms for the short-form prompts; we can accept higher latency for long reports.
- Data residency: US-only. PHI must be isolated and encrypted in transit and at rest. We have a FedRAMP-ish posture but not full FedRAMP.
- Current stack: prototyping on OpenAI API for NLG; we spun up some experiments on an internal k8s GPU cluster for private tests (we saw mixed perf). We are interested in moving production traffic off the public API for cost predictability and auditability.
- Timeline: 6-8 weeks is feasible if we can parallelize security review and network setup.

On hybrid: we like the dedicated + Private VPC approach you suggested. Can Redwood support a canary pattern where we route 10% of traffic to Dedicated for 2 weeks before switching over? Also want to validate token-level cost comparisons vs OpenAI.

Samir (cc'd) is our infra lead and will own the network diagram; he asked that we get SOC2 evidence and a migration checklist so he can sign off.

Available for the technical sync next week: Mon 3/2 10-11am PT or Tue 3/3 1-2pm PT. Which works for you and your SE?

Thanks,
Olivia
VP Product - Acme MedTech
olivia.chen@acme-medtech.com

Subject: Re: Deployment mode and migration plan - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Looping in SE and Solutions to put together a concrete pilot proposal. Marissa - thanks for the clear recap.

Proposed pilot (internal):
- Phase 0 (week 0-2): discovery + security exchange - get Samir the SOC2 summary, migration-checklist.xlsx (attached), and a short list of required network ports and KMS options.
- Phase 1 (week 2-4): Dedicated capacity pilot for non-PHI traffic with 10% canary routing from OpenAI -> Redwood Dedicated to validate latency/cost. David to run bench with representative prompts.
- Phase 2 (week 4-6): Private VPC sandbox for PHI traffic (or dedicated with VPC peering depending on network needs). If everything looks good, expand rollout.

Owners / asks:
- David: run perf/cost bench and produce a short report (throughput, P95, token cost estimate) - target deliverable in 5 business days.
- Vivek: confirm model compatibility (quantization/FP16) and any runtime limits; note any model variants we should recommend for cost/perf tradeoffs.
- Marissa: keep contact with Olivia / Samir and coordinate security exchange + calendar.

I've attached migration-checklist.xlsx to help Samir map out what we need from infra. I'll draft a short mutual action plan and HubSpot task after we confirm the sync time.

Thanks -

Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager - Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone - Mon 3/2 10-11am PT works for me (Olivia confirmed). Please send a calendar invite for that slot and include the following in advance if possible:
- SOC2 summary (we received your stub but need any available evidence links)
- Migration checklist (we got the spreadsheet, thanks)
- A short doc outlining the canary routing plan and rollback steps (we need to present this to our security board)

We are comfortable starting a pilot as early as 3/15 assuming security signoffs. For the canary, we prefer to start at 10% for two weeks, monitor latency and error rates, then move to 50% if stable. If you have a ready-made canary/rollout playbook, please share.

Also cc'ing our infra email infra@acme-medtech.com for operational handoff.
